name: og-spatial-concentration
title: Spatial Concentration: Does a Pore Make an Individual?
concept: Spatial individuation of the protometabolism: whether vent pore physics concentrates a dilute feed strongly enough to ignite the reaction network and form a persistent, localized individual rather than washing into the ocean — one concept studied at several fidelities (thermophoretic concentration physics, full-network pore ignition) as arms.
gate_reason: Gate B (does spatial concentration make an individual). Consolidates the campaign's concentration/individuation line into one concept with explicit fidelity-labelled arms: the thermophoretic concentration physics (og-03) and the full-network pore ignition (og-30, canonical) — each judged against its own matched well-mixed null with feeds held equal. Headline (og-30, canonical): at identical vent-posterior feeds a concentrating mineral pore IGNITES the network (net carbon flux +4.5e-4, 17 persistent species) while a matched well-mixed, non-concentrating control stays dark — spatial concentration is load-bearing, SUPPORTED. Guardrail (kept explicit): the pore benefit is a BOUNDED porosity window, not a broad swath, and network_connected is a brittle proxy near threshold. og-30 does double duty — it meets Gate B and resolves Gate A1's open feed-plausibility question (the pore explains how the A1 carbon-fixing network persists at vent feeds).
claim: Across fidelities, vent pore physics concentrates a dilute feed into a persistent localized individual and ignites the reaction network. Resolving diffusion, thermophoresis, adsorption, surface catalysis and advection, a bounded serpentinite pore clears the Baaske-2007 extreme-accumulation regime (accumulation Peclet 18.4) and localizes a persistent individual vs a well-mixed control (og-03, supported). At identical vent-posterior feeds the concentrating pore ignites the full network — net carbon flux +4.5e-4, 17 persistent species — while a matched well-mixed, non-concentrating control stays dark (og-30, canonical, supported); the C6 network og-29 found needs ~20x well-mixed feed ignites directly in the pore at base feed. The pore benefit is a bounded porosity window, and network_connected is a brittle proxy near threshold (both kept honest). og-30 does double duty: it meets Gate B and resolves Gate A1's feed-plausibility. Consolidated headline: supported — spatial concentration makes the individual and rescues ignition. Every matched null and arm verdict kept.
question: Can vent pore physics concentrate a dilute vent feed strongly enough to form a persistent localized individual and ignite the reaction network productively — more than a matched well-mixed, non-concentrating control at identical feeds?
hypothesis: Bounded-geometry pore physics (thermophoresis + adsorption + advection) concentrates a dilute feed enough to retain a persistent individual and ignite the network, within a bounded porosity window; no individuation or ignition is claimed where a matched well-mixed control matches it.
experiment: Consolidate the spatial-concentration studies into one concept with explicit fidelity-labelled arms (concentration physics, full-network pore ignition), each preserving its matched well-mixed null, verdict, findings and run provenance; report the consolidated verdict (supported) with the bounded-porosity-window guardrail.
result: Vent pore physics concentrates a dilute feed into a persistent localized individual (Baaske regime cleared, accumulation Peclet 18.4) and ignites the full reaction network (net carbon flux +4.5e-4, 17 persistent species) where a matched well-mixed control stays dark (SUPPORTED); the benefit is a bounded porosity window, and og-30 also resolves Gate A1's feed-plausibility.

arms.concept_role: Concentration physics: resolving diffusion, thermophoresis, adsorption, surface catalysis and advection for every actual reactant, a bounded serpentinite pore clears the Baaske-2007 extreme-accumulation regime (accumulation Peclet 18.4) and localizes a persistent individual vs a well-mixed control — a bounded porosity x length region, not a single favourable pair.

Canonical: at identical vent-posterior feeds (CO2/H2 = 1e-3) a concentrating mineral pore IGNITES the full network (net carbon flux +4.5e-4, 17 persistent species) while a matched well-mixed, non-concentrating control stays dark; the C6 network og-29 found needs ~20x well-mixed feed ignites directly in the pore at base feed. Also resolves Gate A1 feed-plausibility. Benefit is a BOUNDED porosity window; network_connected is a brittle proxy near threshold.
Planned benchmark: validate the pore transport/concentration solver against an independent transport reference — does the enrichment hold under a cross-checked solver? (not run)

behavior_tests.name: thermophoretic-enrichment-reproduces-baaske
behavior_tests.description: The thermophoretic trap concentrates the dilute feed. The reduced accumulation column reaches the Baaske-2007 extreme figure (~10^8-fold, Pe_acc ≈ 18.4) in the favorable pore, but that sits ABOVE the demonstrated solver-convergence range: the resolved dolfinx FEM saturates (~10^2-fold) past Pe_acc ≈ 13 (spatial-transport-solver-comparison), so the >10^6 figure is a flow-through reduced-column exp(Pe) extrapolation / closed-cell figure, not a resolved result. Per "no acceptance gate outside demonstrated convergence" the magnitude is REPORTED here, not gated as a pass; localization within the resolvable range (Pe_acc ≲ 13) is the gated claim (see enrichment-resolved-within-convergence).

pass_if.detail: reduced-column Pe_acc ≈ 18.4 (~10^8-fold) reported as the closed-cell/reduced-model figure; the resolved FEM does not confirm it past the convergence-verified Pe_acc ≈ 13

behavior_tests.name: enrichment-resolved-within-convergence
behavior_tests.description: Within the FEM-trustworthy / convergence-verified Péclet range (Pe_acc ≲ 13, spatial-transport-solver-comparison), the resolved thermophoretic field DOES concentrate the feed above its inflow — a bounded individual forms. This is the honest, solver-agnostic localization claim (both FiPy and dolfinx agree in this range); the far larger reduced-column figure above Pe_acc ≈ 13 is reported separately (thermophoretic-enrichment-reproduces-baaske), not gated.

findings.statement: A favorable serpentinite pore (5 mm × 0.1 mm, ΔT 30 K, convective flow) clears the Baaske-2007 extreme-accumulation regime at accumulation Péclet 18.4 from the real thermophoretic + convective transport, with FVM flux conserved to machine epsilon. The corresponding fold-enrichment (reduced-model exp(Pe) ≈ 1e6–1e7, nominally ~9.6×10⁷) is an extrapolation whose magnitude is solver-sensitive above Pe ≈ 13 — the graded quantity is the Péclet, not the precise fold.
findings.explanation: ThermophoreticTrapProcess solves the steady accumulation column; the Péclet is the resolved readout, while the fold-enrichment = exp(beta·L) is a reduced-model extrapolation. A FiPy↔FEniCS head-to-head cross-check finds the two solvers diverge by up to ~5.6 decades at Pe ≳ 13, so the extreme fold-magnitude is not treated as a precise resolved result.

findings.statement: The native pore-localization phase map (porosity × pore length) resolves localization as a bounded region, not a single favourable/open pair: the real trap localizes above the frontier (Péclet ≈ 18, reduced-model fold ≥ 1e6) at 25/144 grid points (~17%), enrichment rising with pore length, while an open pore (porosity→1) and a 10× shorter pore wash the feed through (no localization). The map is native to og-03's own trap readouts — it no longer borrows og-02's feed/washout axes. Localization (an individual forms vs washes through) is robust; the precise fold-magnitude in the high-Péclet interior is solver-sensitive (see limitations).

evidence.observed: 25/144 (17%) localized over (porosity 0.05–0.95 × pore length 5e-4–8e-3 m); open-pore does not concentrate (~1×), 10× shorter pore ~6× — both far below the frontier

findings.explanation: Enrichment rises with pore length and vanishes with confinement/openness — the dilution/localization boundary the campaign sought, read from the real FiPy accumulation solve and rendered as the pore-localization map (Decision view). The frontier LOCATION is robust; the fold-values deep in the high-Péclet interior are a reduced-model extrapolation.

findings.statement: At identical vent-posterior feeds (CO2/H2 = 1e-3), the concentrating pore ignites the network (net carbon flux +4.5e-4; connected; 17 persistent species) while the matched well-mixed nonconcentrating control does not (flux ~0; not connected) - spatial concentration is the only difference, so the pore causes the productive flux.

The C6 network - the one og-29 found ignites only at ~20x well-mixed feed - ignites directly in the demo pore at the vent-posterior base feed (porosity 0.88, pore-local 0.023 M), net carbon flux +4.49e-4, connected, 22 persistent species, while the matched well-mixed C6 control stays dead (flux +1.5e-9, not connected). C6 shows the same bounded-window behavior as C4 - a tight pore (porosity 0.70, pore-local 2.63 M) gives higher flux (+0.072) but the connectivity metric still degrades (network_connected = 0), so there is no flux-washout upper bound; the bound above is physically-implausible feeds plus connectivity-metric degradation, not flux loss.

A porosity sweep shows the pore's benefit is a bounded window, not a broad swath. Net carbon flux rises monotonically with confinement (no flux washout in the C4 network, even at extreme feeds), but the connectivity-defined ignition (og-29's network_connected metric) occupies a bounded, somewhat brittle porosity band (~0.80-0.90; pore-local ~0.01-0.2 M) - below it enrichment is sub-threshold, and above it the pore-local feeds become physically implausible (porosity 0.70 implies 2.6 M, 0.60 implies 36 M) while the connectivity metric itself degrades, flipping 1/0/1 across adjacent porosities at similar high flux. So ignition is met in a specific pore-geometry window, not robustly across geometry.

network_connected (og-29's ignition metric) is a BRITTLE proxy near threshold - at high feed the network stays carbon-fixing (flux high and monotone in enrichment) but loses broad connectivity (connected flips to 0), the same signal og-29 recorded as "washout" at x50 well-mixed, now seen to be connectivity-breadth loss rather than flux loss, consistent across C4/C6 and well-mixed/pore. This is a methodological caveat on the ignition metric only; it does NOT touch og-29's formose refutation, which rests on the thermodynamic mechanism and the coefficient-free seed-independence discriminator, not on connectivity.

This does double duty - it meets Gate B's own criterion (pore flux far exceeds the matched control) and resolves Gate A's open A1 feed-plausibility question: the ~20x well-mixed ignition gap is bridged by pore enrichment within the physical pore window, so a carbon-fixing network persists at vent-realistic feeds inside a pore (demonstrated on C4 and confirmed directly on C6).
